//: What is on a developer's machine after scripts/dev-aws-seed.sh.
THE ADDRESSES ARE COMMITTED AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. Every one ends in
.test, a reserved TLD (RFC 2606) that can never be a real mailbox, so
Cognito can never mail a stranger and nothing is mailed anyway (the
wrapper passes MessageAction SUPPRESS). Keeping them here is what lets
the seeder, the e2e session helper and a human at the sign-in screen
agree on who exists by reading one file. A real mailbox must never
appear here.
NO PASSWORD HERE, and that is the difference between a fixture and a
credential. One password, shared by every person below, lives OUTSIDE
the repo as HUMBUGG_DEV_USER_PASSWORD in
~/.config/andreas-services/humbugg/dev.env: these are throwaway seats
in a pool whose entire contents are this fixture, and one value that
rotates cleanly beats seven that rotate by hand. dev-aws-seed.sh sets it
on every run, so rotating the value converges the accounts instead of
locking them out. HUMBUGG_DEV_USER_EMAIL in the same file should name
one of these people — it is who dev-session.mjs signs the e2e suite in
as.
`handle` names a person for anything that needs to refer to them; the
API never sees it. Keep handles stable — an exchange below refers to
them, and so may a spec.
`exchanges` are created THROUGH THE LOCAL API as the named organizer,
and each participant joins through the organizer's invite link as
themselves — the same two requests the app makes — so a seeded row is a
row the service wrote, never a third hand-rolled copy of an item shape.
An exchange is keyed on (organizer, name): a second run finds the one it
made and joins nobody twice. Rows that already exist are left alone —
a seeded stack is somewhere people work — so a changed exchange is a
new name, not an edit to one that has loaded.
Plans are PER EXCHANGE, not per person. `plan: plus` means the seeder
buys Plus for that exchange the way an organizer does: it opens the
real Stripe TEST Checkout the backend reserves, completes it with the
CLI's tok_visa, and waits for the webhook to land through `stripe
listen`. So the Plus exchange needs dev-up.sh running, not just the
backend.
Why these seven people and two exchanges: the Free plan seats six
(HUMBUGG_FREE_PARTICIPANT_LIMIT, organizer included), so `free-full`
is seeded exactly to the ceiling — the organizer plus five — and
`spare` is the one person deliberately left OUT of it. Sign in as
spare and open free-full's invite link to see the 402 a seventh
participant gets, and sign in as the organizer to see the billing card
say the exchange is full. `plus-exchange` is the same organizer's other
exchange, already on Plus, so managed invitations, co-organizers,
customization and late participants can be tried without buying
anything by hand. Lower HUMBUGG_FREE_PARTICIPANT_LIMIT and the fixture
still loads — the seeder refuses, naming the participant that would
not fit, rather than seeding an exchange that is silently short.
The names and descriptions read as an organizer wrote them, not as
notes to a tester: a participant sees them at the top of their
exchange, and 'Free — full house' told Spare Test about a plan they
had not heard of. The handle carries the test's purpose; the name
does not have to.
In no exchange on purpose. The seventh seat that Free does not have.
